messages:
taylor: Quick check — API contract weirdness: when a stop sequence would be satisfied but max_tokens is hit first, I'm seeing logprobs become null for the last token. Is that expected or a bug?

marco: hmm, that sounds off. We should always return logprobs for generated tokens. Can you paste a minimal repro?

taylor: repro attached inline:
```json
{
  "prompt": "A:\\n1) apple\\n2) banana\\n",
  "max_tokens": 1,
  "stop": ["\\n"],
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "top_p": 1.0,
  "logprobs": 3
}
```
This returns a single token with text "\\n" but logprobs is null.

marco: thanks. Two things to check: 1) runtime currently treats stop sequences as post-generation filters in some code paths (so stop token may be synthesized then dropped), 2) we migrated the logprobs extractor in the last runtime refactor — possible gap.

sophia: timeline note — if we change behavior we must preserve v1 semantics. Some customers rely on null logprobs to detect truncation. Important for backward compatibility.

taylor: good point. From client side POV: null logprobs = truncated vs real low-prob token is ambiguous. We should add explicit metadata instead of relying on null. e.g., add "finish_reason": "max_tokens" / "stop" and keep logprobs consistent.

marco: agree. Proposal: always return logprobs for the final emitted token(s) that came from the model. If we had to remove a stop token by post-filtering, still return the logprobs for the token that triggered stop in a separate field: "filtered_stop_token": {"text": "...", "logprob": -3.2}. That keeps clients unambiguous.

oliver: +1 on explicit finish_reason. Also: edgecase with temperature/top_p interplay — if temperature>0 and top_p<1 the model sampling may pick a token that partial-matches a stop sequence; do we consider prefix matches of stop while sampling?

marco: our sampler operates token-by-token; stop detection occurs on the output string after token appended. So partial matches are only recognized once the full stop token appears (i.e., multi-token stops are checked on concatenated text). If max_tokens stops generation mid-stop sequence, then the stop won't be seen. That is expected but tricky.

sophia: for contract clarity we should document: 1) stops are string-level matches on the emitted character sequence, 2) if max_tokens ends generation before a stop completes, the finish_reason is "max_tokens" and stop is not considered satisfied, 3) logprobs will be provided for any tokens the model actually emitted.

taylor: sounds good. Can we add a small test in runtime unit tests for: multi-token stop + max_tokens= N-1, ensure finish_reason=max_tokens and logprobs present for last emitted token?

marco: I'll add tests. Also pinging CI: tagging job that covers logprob extractor.

ci-bot: build:runtime-logprobs-extractor #242 triggered by @marco — running tests.

oliver: one more ask — update API contract doc (openapi) with explicit finish_reason field (enum: stop, max_tokens, eos, cancelled) and an optional filtered_stop_token object for compatibility. Keep the change behind a minor version bump and add migration note.

sophia: +1. Add a note: clients interpreting null logprobs as truncated should migrate to finish_reason checks.

marco: ok I'll draft the PR: runtime tests + openapi change + changelog. @oliver can you review the openapi changes?

oliver: I'll review today. Also can we add a small example in docs showing stop vs max_tokens behavior and a sample response?

taylor: thanks all. I'll update the SDK shim to surface finish_reason and filtered_stop_token as first-class fields so downstream apps don't break.

marco: ETA: PR by EOD, tests passing locally. If CI green, we'll merge and include a short migration guide in product notes.

ci-bot: build:runtime-logprobs-extractor #242 — tests passed.

taylor: great, thanks! :thumbsup:

oliver: leaving a final note: we should also add an integration test that exercises temperature/top_p diversity with stops to catch sampling cornercases in future refactors.

marco: added to backlog and will create ticket after merge.

sophia: assigning owners: marco (runtime + tests), oliver (openapi + docs), taylor (SDK).
